newsitem.title: USA: Sprint says takeover by C&W impossible.
newsitem.headline: Sprint says takeover by C&W impossible.

text.p: Sprint Corp quoted its chief executive William Esrey as saying that a takeover bid for the company by Cable and Wireless Plc supported by France Telecom would not be possible.

"A reported deal by Cable & Wireless, supported by France Telecom, could not be possible because of the terms of a standstill agreement Sprint has with France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom," a Sprint spokesman quoted Esrey as saying.
France Telecom has separately denied the story, which was reported in the Wall Street Journal.
Esrey was at a Merrill Lynch conference, where Sprint said he originally made the remarks. Sprint said it did not normally comment on speculation.

The Wall Street Journal said C&W was considering a bid for the 80 percent of Sprint that is not already owned by Sprint's two European partners in the Global One alliance, and had talked with France Telecom to get its support.
France Telecom earlier denied the report. It said its talks with C&W were over the possibility of C&W becoming the British partner in Global One.
Global One, set up early in 1996, is a one-stop shop for corporate telecommunication needs and acts as a carrier of international traffic for other telecom firms.
Sprint shares were 1-1/2 higher at 44-5/8 at 1145 EST/1645 GMT, and Cable & Wireless American Depositary Receipts were 1/8 higher at 24-1/8.
Sprint stock was earlier halted on the New York Stock Exchange for an imbalance, and C&W's ADRs were halted for dissemination, the NYSE said. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
